text:
Priya (AE): Heads-up - Northlane Systems POC hitting disconnects on their SSE proxy. They use our Go SDK and see sessions dropped after ~75s idle. They need guidance: keepalive pattern, whether pings count as tokens, and recommended ephemeral token TTL for connector rotation.

Luis (Solutions): Short: use transport-level keepalive (SSE comment ping or TCP keepalive). Those do NOT count as model tokens. Only inference calls consume tokens. If their proxy can be configured to a longer idle timeout that's best.

Ben (Runtime Eng): Confirmed. Transport pings are orthogonal to our batching/generation path. Caveat: some Dedicated clusters enforce idle teardown at infra level (~2m) — reach out if you need a temporary relax. Also reconnects that re-send full system prompt to re-warm the KV cache will incur token cost.

Priya (AE): If they send a tiny empty generation as a keepalive to avoid reconnect, would that increase cost or affect latency/batching?

Ben (Runtime Eng): That would count as a generation and go through batching, so yes it would cost tokens and potentially slightly change latency characteristics. Use transport pings instead.

Nora (Presales): They want 5 minute short-lived creds to rotate per connector refresh. Is that supported and any gotchas?

Luis (Solutions): 5m is supported but aggressive. We recommend 10-15m for POCs to reduce refresh storms and timing edge-cases. If they use 5m, implement jittered refresh and exponential backoff on refresh failures. Example curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/refresh \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <refresh-token>" \
  -d '{"scope":"inference"}'
```
Add 10-30s random jitter to rotation.

Priya (AE): Can you paste a short Go snippet for SSE ping and a note about not re-warming full context on reconnect?

Luis (Solutions): Go pseudo-example for SSE client ping (keepalive handled by transport):
```go
// net/http Transport keepalive tweak
tr := &http.Transport{IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
resp, _ := client.Get("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream")
// server side SSE comments or periodic ping frames are OK
```
And note: if connector on reconnect replays long system messages to rehydrate state, they'll pay for those tokens. Recommend storing a minimal checkpoint (conversation IDs + small context) and only rehydrate deltas.

deploy-bot: FYI - filed ticket to eng-runtime to review Dedicated idle policy for this POC (ticket: RDI-4532).

Ben (Runtime Eng): Also watch when using structured tool-calls: some clients reload tool metadata on each reconnect which can trigger model lookups. Cache tool schemas locally or upstream to avoid repeated regen.

Priya (AE): Pricing Q from Northlane: do POCs have a minimum or reserved option to cap spend?

Nora (Presales): Default is PAYG. For predictable high-throughput evals we can offer a short reserved trial — ask them to DM estimated QPS and hours and I'll draft a trial commitment.

Luis (Solutions): Handoff checklist summary I can prepare: 1) Use transport keepalive (SSE/TCP) not noop generations; 2) 5m ephemeral tokens supported but 10-15m recommended; 3) add jitter to refresh cadence; 4) avoid re-sending full long prompts on reconnect — use checkpointing; 5) cache tool schemas locally for structured output; 6) contact eng-runtime for temporary idle policy changes.

Priya (AE): Please create the one-page checklist and I'll attach to the POC handoff. I'll also request proxy logs from Northlane and ask them to try increasing idle timeout. Thanks all :partyparrot:
